title: Pattern Matching using Brute Force
description: Given a text string and a pattern string, find the first starting index of the pattern in the text using the Brute Force algorithm. If the pattern is not found, return -1.
inputFormat: First line contains the text string. Second line contains the pattern string.
outputFormat: Integer representing the 0-based index of the first match, or -1.
note: Both strings consist of lowercase English letters.

title: KMP Pattern Matching
description: Implement the Knuth-Morris-Pratt (KMP) algorithm to find all occurrences of a pattern in a text. Return the starting indices separated by space. If none, return -1.
inputFormat: First line: text. Second line: pattern.
outputFormat: Space-separated integers of starting indices or -1.
note: Text length <= 10^5, pattern length <= 10^5.

title: Infix to Postfix Conversion
description: Convert a given infix mathematical expression to a postfix expression using a stack.
inputFormat: A single string representing the infix expression (without spaces).
outputFormat: A single string representing the postfix expression.
note: Supported operators: +, -, *, /, ^. Parentheses may be present. Operands are single letters.

title: Postfix Expression Evaluation
description: Evaluate a given postfix expression containing single digit operands and basic operators (+, -, *, /, %).
inputFormat: A single string representing the postfix expression.
outputFormat: An integer representing the evaluated result.
note: Assume valid postfix expression and division by zero will not occur.

title: Circular Queue Operations
description: Implement a Circular Queue of size N. Perform a series of Enqueue (E x) and Dequeue (D) operations. Print the queue elements from front to rear after all operations.
inputFormat: First line: N (queue size) and Q (number of operations). Next Q lines: operations (E x or D).
outputFormat: Space-separated integers representing the queue content. If empty, print 'Empty'.
note: Ignore Dequeue if empty, ignore Enqueue if full.

title: Doubly Ended Queue
description: Implement a Deque. Operations: Insert Front (IF x), Insert Rear (IR x), Delete Front (DF), Delete Rear (DR). Print elements from front to rear after Q operations.
inputFormat: First line: Q (operations count). Next Q lines: operations.
outputFormat: Space-separated elements of the deque.
note: The deque can grow infinitely.

title: Priority Queue using Arrays
description: Implement a Priority Queue using an array. Perform insertions and extract max operations. Print the max elements extracted.
inputFormat: First line: Q (operations). Next Q lines: I x (insert x) or E (extract max).
outputFormat: For each E operation, print the extracted max value.
note: Print 'Empty' if E is called on an empty queue.

title: SLL Front Insertion
description: Insert N elements to the front of a Singly Linked List. Print the list elements after all insertions.
inputFormat: First line: N. Second line: N space-separated integers.
outputFormat: Space-separated integers representing the SLL.
note: Since elements are inserted at the front, they will appear in reverse order of input.

title: Count Nodes in SLL
description: Given elements to append to a SLL, write a function to count the number of nodes in the SLL.
inputFormat: First line: N (number of elements). Second line: N elements.
outputFormat: An integer representing the count of nodes.
note: Do not just print N, implement the SLL and count.

title: DLL End Insertion
description: Create a Doubly Linked List by inserting N elements at the end. Print the list forwards and backwards.
inputFormat: First line: N. Second line: N elements.
outputFormat: Two lines: First line forwards, Second line backwards.
note: DLL nodes should have prev and next pointers.

title: Polynomial Addition using Linked List
description: Add two polynomials represented by linked lists. Each term has a coefficient and an exponent. Print the resulting polynomial.
inputFormat: First line N (terms in Poly1). Next N lines: coeff exp. Next line M. Next M lines: coeff exp.
outputFormat: Resulting polynomial terms in descending order of exponents: coeff exp ...
note: Add coefficients of matching exponents. Do not print terms with 0 coefficient.

title: Reverse a Singly Linked List
description: Given a Singly Linked List, reverse it in-place and print the new list.
inputFormat: First line: N. Second line: N elements to be inserted at the end.
outputFormat: Space-separated elements of the reversed list.
note: Use O(1) auxiliary space.

title: Josephus Problem via Circular Linked List
description: Solve the Josephus problem using a Circular Linked List. Given N people standing in a circle and a step count K, find the survivor.
inputFormat: First line: N and K.
outputFormat: Integer representing the survivor (1-based index).
note: Person 1 to N. Count K people and eliminate the K-th person. Repeat.

title: Binary Tree Traversals
description: Given the array representation of a complete binary tree (1-based index), print its Inorder, Preorder, and Postorder traversals.
inputFormat: First line: N. Second line: N elements.
outputFormat: Three lines: Inorder, Preorder, and Postorder space-separated elements.
note: Left child of i is 2*i, right child is 2*i + 1.

title: Maximum Depth of a Complete Binary Tree
description: Find the maximum depth (height) of a complete binary tree given its array representation.
inputFormat: First line: N. Second line: N elements.
outputFormat: An integer representing the height (root is at height 1).
note: Height is the number of nodes along the longest path from root to leaf.

title: Print all Root to Leaf Paths
description: Given a complete binary tree in array form, print all paths from the root to the leaves, one path per line.
inputFormat: First line: N. Second line: N elements.
outputFormat: Paths, each on a new line, nodes separated by spaces. Paths should be printed from left to right.
note: A leaf is a node with no children.

title: Binary Search Tree Creation
description: Create a BST by inserting N elements in the given order. Print its Inorder traversal to verify it is sorted.
inputFormat: First line: N. Second line: N integers.
outputFormat: Space-separated integers of the Inorder traversal.
note: Insert into BST without self-balancing.

title: Evaluate Binary Expression Tree
description: Given a postfix expression, build an expression tree and then evaluate it to return the result.
inputFormat: A single string postfix expression with single-digit operands.
outputFormat: The evaluated integer result.
note: Operators: +, -, *, /

title: Search in a BST
description: Insert N elements into a BST. Then, given Q queries, print 'Found' or 'Not Found' for each query.
inputFormat: First line N. Second line N integers. Third line Q. Next Q lines: query integers.
outputFormat: For each query, print 'Found' or 'Not Found' on a new line.

title: Construct MAX-Heap
description: Given N elements, build a MAX-Heap and print the array representation of the heap.
inputFormat: First line N. Second line N elements.
outputFormat: Space-separated elements of the MAX-Heap.
note: Insert elements one by one and heapify up.

title: Delete from MAX-Heap
description: Build a MAX-Heap from N elements. Perform Q delete (extract max) operations. Print the array representation of the heap after operations.
inputFormat: First line N. Second line N elements. Third line Q.
outputFormat: Space-separated elements of the remaining MAX-Heap.
note: Replace root with last element and heapify down.

title: Hashing with Linear Probing
description: Implement a Hash Table of size M using Linear Probing for collision resolution. Hash function: H(k) = k % M. Insert N elements and print the final table. Empty slots should print -1.
inputFormat: First line M and N. Second line N elements.
outputFormat: M space-separated integers representing the hash table.
note: If table is full, insertion fails (silently ignore).

title: Hashing with Chaining
description: Implement a Hash Table of size M using Chaining. Hash function: H(k) = k % M. Insert N elements. Print the elements of each bucket separated by spaces. Empty buckets print 'Empty'.
inputFormat: First line M and N. Second line N elements.
outputFormat: M lines, i-th line contains the elements in bucket i.
note: Append new elements to the end of the chain.

title: AVL Tree Balance Factor
description: Insert N elements into a standard BST. For each node in the BST, calculate its Balance Factor (Height of Left Subtree - Height of Right Subtree). Print the node values and their balance factors in Inorder traversal.
inputFormat: First line N. Second line N elements.
outputFormat: N lines, each with 'value balance_factor'.
note: Height of an empty subtree is 0.

title: Red-Black Tree Properties Check
description: Given a BST, verify if it satisfies the properties of a Red-Black Tree. (Given node colors).
inputFormat: First line N. Next N lines: value color ('R' or 'B').
outputFormat: 'Yes' if it is a valid Red-Black Tree, else 'No'.
note: Root must be black, no red node can have a red child, all paths from node to descendants have same number of black nodes.

title: Graph BFS Traversal
description: Given an unweighted directed graph with N vertices and M edges, perform a Breadth First Search starting from vertex 0. Print the visited vertices.
inputFormat: First line N and M. Next M lines contain edges u v.
outputFormat: Space-separated vertices in BFS order.
note: Visit adjacent vertices in ascending numerical order.

title: Graph DFS Traversal
description: Given an unweighted directed graph with N vertices and M edges, perform a Depth First Search starting from vertex 0. Print the visited vertices.
inputFormat: First line N and M. Next M lines contain edges u v.
outputFormat: Space-separated vertices in DFS order.
note: Visit adjacent vertices in ascending numerical order.

title: Detect Cycle in a Directed Graph
description: Given a directed graph, output 'Yes' if it contains a cycle, else 'No'.
inputFormat: First line N and M. Next M lines contain edges u v.
outputFormat: 'Yes' or 'No'.
note: Use DFS and a recursion stack to detect back edges.

title: Path between Two Vertices
description: Given a directed graph and two vertices S and D, determine if there is a path from S to D.
inputFormat: First line N and M. Next M lines contain edges u v. Last line contains S and D.
outputFormat: 'Yes' or 'No'.
note: Use BFS or DFS.

title: Disjoint Sets Union-Find
description: Implement a Disjoint Set data structure with N elements. Operations: Union(u, v) and Find(u, v). Find should output 'Yes' if u and v are in the same set, else 'No'.
inputFormat: First line N and Q. Next Q lines: operations (U u v or F u v).
outputFormat: For each F operation, print 'Yes' or 'No' on a new line.
note: Elements are 0-indexed.
